channel.title: The Git Reporter
channel.description: A code-native newspaper of meaningful software change.

item.title: The Approval Arrived. The Subagent Could Not Continue.
item.description: Microsoft’s Agent Framework closes a misleading route through delegated tool approval. A child can decide immediately under policy; a person who answers later needs a workflow that knows where to return.

item.title: API Discovery: Shorten the Context, Keep the History
item.description: Pi v0.87.0 lets a builder append an edit to future model context while leaving the original transcript intact. That is useful for a reading assistant—and it is not data deletion.

item.title: Builder Work: The Last Writer Is Not the Last Run
item.description: CrewAI’s new evaluation shortcut needs a trustworthy pointer to completed work. The hard part is deciding which run deserves the file when exports and writers arrive out of order.

item.title: OpenClaw Had Stopped the Child. Restart Brought Back the Parent.
item.description: A waiting conversation could survive its own cancellation in OpenClaw’s recovery records. A new repair saves the parent’s stopped state before answering the user—and protects a newer turn from that delayed write.

item.title: API Discovery: Let the Agent Pick a Record You Already Have
item.description: Pydantic AI’s new Choices helper builds a menu from data available at run time. The model selects a validated key; the application gets back the record that key represents.

item.title: Builder Work: No Score Is a Result Worth Preserving
item.description: Mastra’s agent-assisted evaluation work gives an irrelevant run a separate outcome. The difficult part is carrying that distinction all the way to storage, averages and the final verdict.

item.title: Qwen Code Stops Calling a Rerun a Resume
item.description: Two September 18 changes separate a recoverable interruption from a fresh start: refuse a missing journal, then make the interrupted run visible. Neither promises automatic recovery.

item.title: API Discovery: Let the Speaker Finish Before You Close
item.description: Pydantic AI adds a session-level wait between a generated reply and closing the voice connection. The audio consumer still has to tell the truth about playback.

item.title: Builder Work: The Underscore That Rewound Another Agent
item.description: An OpenWorker patch attributed to Devin protects a neighboring workspace during a database migration. Its strongest lesson is the assertion about the row that should not move.

item.title: Unsloth Rolled Back the Sandbox Its Review Had Just Cleared
item.description: A live review reported working Linux and macOS isolation. The next day, the implementation was reverted. Studio’s remaining protections make the consequence more specific than “the sandbox is gone.”

item.title: API Discovery: Build a Reading Test with Questions That Have No Answer
item.description: Hugging Face’s Dataset Viewer can select labelled unanswerable questions before you download a corpus. Keep those labels out of the model’s input.

item.title: Builder Work: Keep the Failure Useful and the Payload Out of the Log
item.description: LangChain’s new TypeSafe client gives application code detailed failures and ordinary log messages a smaller view. The engineering lesson lies in the boundary between them.

item.title: The Allow Button Was Waiting for a Socket
item.description: OpenWork reproduced a ten-second approval timeout before the user’s decision reached the engine. The repair gives that decision a separate route through a busy desktop app.

item.title: API Discovery: Keep the Query Handle, Not the Connection
item.description: Snowflake’s SQL API gives unfinished work a receipt. Save it, check it later, and keep “accepted” separate from “results ready.”

item.title: Builder Work: Keep the Empty Object Open
item.description: An agent-assisted LangChain fix protects a gateway’s free-form arguments. The useful craft is testing what a schema means after another library has translated it.

item.title: The Cookie Jar Between Two Agent Sessions
item.description: Microsoft’s Agent Framework is changing what its Python HTTP clients remember. A new conversation can still inherit an old login when both use the same cookie jar.

item.title: API Discovery: Tell a Running Pydantic Agent What Just Changed
item.description: Pydantic AI’s enqueue API lets a worker add context while an agent is running. A September 15 repair makes the closing boundary explicit: the message enters the queue, or the caller gets an error.

item.title: Builder Work: Headlong Puts Its Runtime Out of Reach
item.description: A persistent agent needs somewhere to experiment without rewriting the machinery that keeps it alive. Headlong’s systemd deployment draws that line—and its migration shows why the line is harder than a read-only flag.

item.title: The Fine Print Behind Kilo’s Swarm Default
item.description: Kilo’s main branch now enables a shared agent board by default. Its messages can carry findings across a team—but a successful post cannot summon a worker, prove it listened, or stop it.

item.title: API Discovery: Give the Reviewer Fewer Tools Than the Builder
item.description: Qwen Code’s workflow API can set one agent’s reasoning effort and remove tools from that step. Those choices also change which saved result a resumed workflow may reuse.

item.title: Builder Work: Save the Good Citation Before the Reviewer Times Out
item.description: Shepherd’s citation checker keeps complete results through a failed review batch. The useful craft lies in deciding what can survive—and what must remain untrusted.

item.title: A Child Agent Can't Promise Its Watcher to the Parent
item.description: Hermes now makes a child wait, kill, or formally hand over background work before it returns—ending one treacherous kind of progress report.

item.title: API Discovery: Let a Pydantic AI Agent Use Your Codex Subscription
item.description: Pydantic AI’s new Codex provider turns an existing subscription into a typed-agent option—with its authentication and streaming limits in plain view.

item.title: Builder Work: Let the Author Lookup Fail Without Losing the Feedback
item.description: Mastra’s agent-assisted feedback work makes identity a useful optional layer—not a reason to lose an anonymous or unresolved record.

item.title: A Computer-Using Agent Needs a Room, Not a House Key
item.description: OpenWork’s merged macOS 14+ preview gives a desktop-driving agent one person-approved window and a short-lived native session—a meaningful boundary, but not an operating-system sandbox.

item.title: API Discovery: A Free Search MCP Still Has a Destination
item.description: Microsoft Agent Framework now shows how to call Parallel Search MCP without an API key—a useful public-web research path, provided the researcher treats every query, URL, objective, and session ID as data leaving the client.

item.title: No Mail Server Is Not a Free Pass
item.description: QM’s new admin-login route lets an already authorized administrator open a portal before outbound email exists—but only through a five-minute, origin-bound, one-use handoff that gets checked again at the door.

item.title: API Discovery: A Shared Agent Thread Needs an Author Field
item.description: Mastra’s MASTRA_MESSAGE_AUTHOR_KEY lets a server carry a verified sender into stored shared-agent messages—useful for accountability, as long as no one mistakes attribution for authorization.

item.title: Builder Work: Make an Agent’s Wake-Up Note a Contract
item.description: Headlong turns a persistent coding agent’s reorientation into a versioned wake context—runtime SHA, sync time, and a bounded workspace map—so the first step after a pause need not be another pwd / ls ritual.

item.title: An Agent’s ‘No’ Needs a Way Back—But Not a Shortcut
item.description: Qwen Code now offers one manual review only for the exact action its AUTO mode blocked—turning a false positive into an accountable decision instead of a workaround hunt.
